answer: Each agent seals a 4 GB replica bound to its public key with a Quartz pass, Argon2id at 1 GiB memory plus a 20-minute sequential delay, so the bytes cannot be copied between identities. Every epoch an Opal beacon draws 32 random chunks and demands Merkle openings within 300 ms, which blocks fetching data on demand. A replica that misses two audits becomes a relic and its 25 token bond is slashed. Cloning 10,000 identities needs 40 TB of disk, about 3,300 sealing hours, and 250,000 tokens at risk; a swarm that cheats resembles a foundry recasting every bell after each inspection.
